newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end moderately lower at midday.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end moderately lower at midday.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended the Friday morning session only moderately down after bouncing off deeper lows brought about by interest rate jitters at the start of trading, brokers said.
"The rebound is still quite fragile," said K.L. Wong, sales manager at Core Pacific Securities.
The Hang Seng Index finished the morning sesson 35.00 points down at 12,437.33 after falling more than 140 points at the open to a low of 12,331.63.
Turnover remained heavy at HK$6.16 billion, well above Thursday morning's HK$4.96 billion.

The market has more than discounted a 25 basis point rise in interest rates, widely expected to be announced after the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next Tuesday, said Wong.

The local market took its cue at the open from Wall Street, where the Dow industrials fell 57.40 points to 6,820.28 after Fed chief Alan Greenspan warned U.S. wage increases would not remain on a lower upward track than inflation indefinitely.
"This is just a technical rebound," said Tony Yung, research manager at Tai Fook Securities. "I am still cautious on the near-term outlook."
But brokers said the market was buoyed somewhat by large overseas houses placing large orders for major blue chips
Interest-rate sensitive utilities led the market down, followed by banks. Hongkong Telecom lost HK$0.10 to HK$14.35 and China Light dropped HK$0.20 to HK$34.00.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings was heavily traded. The share dipped to a low of HK$174.00 but then recovered to end the session HK$1.00 lower at HK$176.50 on heavy turnover of HK$737.96 million.
Cheung Kong ended unchanged at HK$67.25 on trade of HK$651.53 million.
Red chips took the worst beating.

"People have been buying the concept of assets injections by the parent company (into the Hong Kong-listed subsidiary), and now investors worry these injections won't be approved by the Chinese government," said Wong.
Red chip favourite Shanghai Industrial lost HK$1.30 to HK$32.40. The company reported 1996 earnings of HK$360 million, its first annual report since listing.
"The (company's earnings) results were good but when they failed to announce asset injections at the same time, investors got nervous," said Wong. -- Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
